a100-80gb.name: NVIDIA A100 80GB SXM
a100-80gb.notes: Datasheet SXM column: FP16/BF16 Tensor Core 312 TF (624 with sparsity*), INT8 624 TOPS (1,248 with sparsity*), 80GB, 2,039 GB/s. Ampere has no FP8 tensor cores.

h100-sxm.name: NVIDIA H100 SXM
h100-sxm.notes: NVIDIA lists only sparse numbers: FP16/BF16 1,979 TFLOPS*, FP8 3,958*, INT8 3,958 TOPS*, 80GB, 3.35TB/s (*with sparsity). Dense = half, per the NVIDIA H100 datasheet footnote 'Specifications 1/2 lower without sparsity' (NVIDIA doc 2569583, copy hosted at https://bxin.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/products/collateral/servers-unified-computing/ucs-c-series-rack-servers/nvidia-h100-80-gpu.pdf).

rtx-4090.name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090
rtx-4090.notes: Ada whitepaper Appendix A, Table 2 (dense / sparse): FP16 Tensor with FP32 accumulate 165.2 / 330.4, FP16 Tensor with FP16 accumulate 330.3 / 660.6, INT8 Tensor 660.6 / 1321.2 TOPS, 24 GB GDDR6X, 1008 GB/s. This project uses the FP32-accumulate number because PyTorch/cuBLAS GEMMs accumulate in FP32. FP8 was not checked, so it is left empty.

gaudi2.name: Intel Gaudi 2
gaudi2.notes: Memory 96 GB HBM2E at 2.45 TB/s: Gaudi 2 whitepaper. Matrix engine (MME) peaks BF16 432 TFLOPS and FP8 865 TFLOPS: Table 1 of the Intel Gaudi 3 white paper (https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/817486/gaudi-3-ai-accelerator-white-paper.pdf), which lists Gaudi 2 bandwidth as 2.46 TB/s. Intel does not say whether these are dense or sparse; treated as dense (assumption). The BF16 number is stored in the fp16 slot (same 16-bit math). No INT8 MME number is published, so 8-bit runs use FP8.
